evidence.supportingExcerpt: The nucleus houses most cellular DNA; mitochondria have their own genome and participate in energy metabolism and other processes. Ribosomes make polypeptide chains. The endoplasmic reticulum and Golgi process and sort selected membrane or secreted cargo, while lysosomes degrade delivered material in an acidic compartment. That itinerary is not the route of every protein. Cytosol is the fluid outside membrane-bound organelle interiors; cytoplasm includes cytosol and structures outside the nucleus. A vesicle lumen is not cytosol.

A nucleus has an inner and an outer membrane, pores and DNA associated with proteins as chromatin. Rough endoplasmic reticulum forms a membrane network with a lumen; its membrane connects with the outer nuclear membrane. The Golgi consists of flattened membrane sacs, while a lysosome encloses material for breakdown. A mitochondrion has outer and inner membranes; folds of the inner membrane are cristae, and the matrix lies inside it. Its genome is distinct from nuclear chromatin. This general description is not an inventory of every human cell subtype, nor proof that DNA can never occur elsewhere.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: DNA methylation changes a base’s chemical state without substituting the underlying sequence letter. Much human methylation analysis concerns 5-methylcytosine at CpG sites. Histone modifications affect DNA-associated proteins and are distinct from marks on DNA itself. Some regulatory states persist through division; epigenetic does not mean every mark is permanent or transmitted between generations. Promoter methylation can participate in reduced transcription, while patterns elsewhere need their own interpretation.

In an invented sequence example, AACGT can carry a methyl group on its C while the underlying base order remains AACGT. Replacing that C with T instead gives AATGT, a different underlying DNA sequence. Changing a chemical mark on a histone protein is different again. Keep that biological comparison separate from an assay that chemically converts bases: standard bisulfite treatment can change the readout without establishing that the original DNA carried a C-to-T variant. Read the conversion chemistry, locus and cell context before interpreting a methylation call.

Imagine separate precursor RNAs from the same fictional gene, with exons A, B and C in that order. One processing outcome retains A-B-C; another joins A directly to C. B is a skipped exon in the second outcome, rather than a region reclassified as an intron. One RNA molecule is not split into both complete products. These are selected outcomes across separate molecules, with other processing possibilities left open. Retained exon sequence can include untranslated regions. The letter pattern alone supplies neither a reading frame nor a guarantee about protein production or RNA decay.

semanticAssessment.explanation: The exact field separates a local junction read from a complete transcript and protein consequences. Tumour/cell attribution and benefit are unresolved reading boundaries; no new assay performance or empirical benefit is inferred.
semanticAssessment.sourceScope: Complete actual abstracts or individually logged targeted official/review passages and two Dostie PDF pages; no whole primary-paper/protocol or wholesale baseline-claim verification.
semanticAssessment.constructionPremises: Toy examples are hypothetical; colors, geometry, counts and arrows are schematic conventions, not biological frequencies or approval/clinical evidence.
